correctness.rationale: For every connected noncomplete strongly regular graph, the adjacency identity \(A^2=(d-\mu)I+(\lambda-\mu)A+\mu J\) yields precisely two nonconstant adjacency eigenvalues. The nonaccelerated branch follows from the nonnegative low-mode factor. The accelerated branch follows from an explicit positive convex combination of the two spectral products whose bilinear interpolation is \(R_*+(1-R_*)(1-dp)(1-dq)\), globally lower-bounding the maximum modulus. Equality forces unique gains, the zero-eigenvalue boundary has a separate proof, and multiplication using the adjacency identity establishes the mean-field formula. A standalone standard-library verifier passed 20,687 assertions on eight graph examples built from explicit edge predicates; this does not replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: A natural network consensus design problem with per-step transition nonnegativity receives an exact graph-wide solution. The threshold compares adjacent versus nonadjacent common-neighbor numbers; it yields unique implementable optimal transition rates, strict schedule improvement for nontrivial families such as Petersen and Clebsch, and exact finite-time mean-field mixing for balanced multipartite graphs. This classification is not merely a parameter table, restated spectral formula or unsupported finite example.
